title: Adaptive latency-cost tradeoff autoscaler policy for dedicated fleets
creator: Amira Chen
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleet customers require strict throughput guarantees while minimizing cost and preserving latency SLOs across heterogeneous tenant workloads. Current autoscalers target single metrics (p95 latency or token throughput) and either overshoot capacity for tail workloads or oscillate under bursty arrival patterns.

Goal: Design and implement an autoscaling policy engine that natively optimizes a latency-vs-cost tradeoff metric, supports per-tenant throughput guarantees, enforces safety limits (step size, cooldowns, budget caps), and integrates with Dedicated routing and fallback policies. The policy must be configurable per-fleet and expose observability to SLO failure reasons (headroom shortage, cold-start, KV-cache miss amplification).

Target metrics: p95 and p99 request latency (ms) weighted by tenant SLA tier, effective token/sec (aggregate and per-tenant), GPU utilization percentage (per-machine and per-fleet), and queued request depth. We will compute a single composite objective: cost_penalty * delta_cost + latency_penalty * exceedance_ms, with tunable coefficients per-customer.

Scaling algorithms: primary controller is a hybrid of a predictive workload forecaster (seasonal ETS + lightweight LSTM ensemble for burst detection) producing a 60s horizon, and a closed-loop PI controller over the composite objective for short-term corrections. The controller implements: 1) safe max step (percent increase/decrease cap per update), 2) derivative damping to avoid oscillation, 3) per-tenant fairshare allocator that converts fleet-level scale decisions into per-pool provisioning targets, and 4) an emergency fallback policy that temporarily prioritizes high-SLA tenants and stalls batchable low-priority requests when headroom is insufficient.

Safety limits and policy constraints: - max_step_up: 30% of current fleet capacity per minute - max_step_down: 20% per minute with additional hysteresis window - cooldown: 45s after a scale event before another growth event, 120s before a shrink when utilization low - budget_cap: per-tenant reserved credit throttle from Dedicated contract - floor_capacity: minimum nodes to keep for cold-start prevention - surge_quota: short-window temporary burst capacity from shared pool subject to cost-signoff.

Integration points: routing policy must be annotated by the autoscaler with capacity signals so Console can reflect expected headroom and preemptible capacity. KV cache warmup metrics will be used as a modifier to the latency_penalty when cache_miss_rate > 0.6. Autoscaler will call the runtime's scale API and also emit a proposed scaling plan to the rollout orchestrator for canary validation in Dedicated test pools.

Observability: new dashboards for composite objective, per-tenant headroom, forecast error, action history (scale up/down events with step size and reasoning), and incident links. Evals to detect regressions on quality when quantization/eviction policies change.

Deliverables: design doc, implementation in autoscale service, integration tests in staging, observability dashboards, and migration plan for existing Dedicated fleets.
acceptance_criteria: Composite objective implemented and configurable via fleet policy
Autoscaler passes integration tests under synthetic burst scenarios (95th percentile of historical bursts) without SLO violations for high-tier tenants
Safety limits enforced for both increase and decrease operations and validated via chaos tests
Console shows per-fleet headroom estimates and last-proposed scaling actions
Cost vs latency tradeoff documented with recommended coefficient defaults for tiers
design_decisions: Use hybrid predictive + PI controller to balance forecast optimism and closed-loop correction
Expose composite objective coefficients as fleet policy knobs rather than hard-coding thresholds
Limit max_step_up to avoid large immediate cost spikes and set stricter limits on scale-down to prefer stability
Prioritize high-SLA tenants in emergency fallback to meet contractual guarantees
Emit proposed plans to rollout orchestrator for additional validation before destructive downsizes
experiments: Staging experiment #1: ETS-only forecast underestimates burst peaks by 18% in 30s horizon -> hybrid improves to 6%
Staging experiment #3: PI-only controller produced oscillations with 12s period under sinusoidal load; adding derivative damping reduced oscillation amplitude by 80%
Cost simulation: enforcing max_step_up 30% reduced peak spend by ~22% across synthetic workloads while increasing short tail latency by 6ms for P3 tenants
